The status of individual lymph nodes in these 122 patients was also evaluated. During mediastinoscopy, six hundred and twenty lymph nodes were collected from the mediastinum. Lymph nodes from 47 frozen sections were positive. source: Metronidazole and tetracycline prevent liver damage associated with small intestinal bacterial overgrowth in rats. Bacterial overgrowth of the small intestine, following the surgical creation of empty self-filling loops, leads to the development of hepatobiliary lesions in susceptible strains of rats. The pathogenesis of the lesions has been linked to luminal bacteria or their cell wall polymers, whereas rats operated on sham or provided with empty self-draining loops, showing a slight increase in bacterial numbers, did not develop liver lesions. In this study, antibiotics with different spectrums of activity were administered continuously from the day or 22 days after surgery to identify which intestinal flora might be responsible for the development of liver injury in rats with small intestinal bacterial overgrowth. Four weeks after surgery, Lewis rats with untreated self-filling empty loops had elevated liver histologic scores (8.2 +/- 1.3 vs. 0.7 +/- 0.4) and plasma aspartate aminotransferase levels (269 +/- 171 vs. 84 +/- 24) compared to sham-operated rats (P < 0.001). Oral gentamicin as well as oral and intraperitoneal polymyxin B, which binds endotoxin, did not prevent liver damage in rats with self-filling empty loops. However, oral treatment with metronidazole and tetracycline, administered continuously from 1 day after surgery, decreased liver damage (histological score 3.0 +/- 1.8, 2.9 +/- 1.1; aspartate aminotransferase levels 87 +/- 25, 98 +/- 34; respectively P < 0.001 compared to empty loops unprocessed self-filling files). The prognostic significance of pretreatment bone marrow cytogenetic studies in adults with acute lymphocytic leukemia, treated at a single institution with an identical treatment schedule, is described. A total of 105 patients with a documented morphological diagnosis of acute lymphocytic leukemia were examined for this analysis. Cytogenetic analysis was performed in 103 patients, using the Giemsa strip technique with trypsin pretreatment on cells in 24-hour culture, after a thorough workup at presentation that all patients underwent. The specific cytogenetic classification in the 103 patients who had the karyotypic analysis was as follows: diploid 27%; hyperdiploid 12%; B cell karyotype 6%; 6q- and 14q+ anomalies 4%; pseudodiploid 8%; hypodiploid 2%; and insufficient metaphases 28%; Philadelphia chromosome positive 13%. Philadelphia chromosome-positive, B-cell, 6q-, or 14q+ karyotypes tended to be correlated with other known negative prognostic factors. Patients with diploid, hyperdiploid, pseudodiploid, hypodiploid karyotypes or with insufficient metaphases could be grouped into a single group with a favorable prognosis. In this group, the remission rate with induction chemotherapy was 89%, the median duration of complete remission was 26 months, the median survival was 25 months, and the 3-year survival rate was 45%. Patients with positive Philadelphia chromosome, B cell, and 6q- or 14q+ abnormalities collectively had an unfavorable prognosis. Their response rate to induction chemotherapy was 65%, the median duration of response was 7 months, the median survival was 8 months, and the 3-year survival rate was less than 10%. We conclude that pretreatment bone marrow karyotype is an important part of the evaluation of adults with acute lymphocytic leukemia and provides meaningful prognostic information.

That excimer laser coronary angioplasty can remove atherosclerotic intracoronary tissue has been demonstrated. In a 53-year-old white man with 90% stenosis of the left anterior descending coronary artery and exertional angina (Canadian Cardiovascular Society class III), autonomous coronary angioplasty with excimer laser was successfully performed. Through the use of a 1.2 mm then 1.8 mm diameter laser catheter, the lesion was reduced to a residual stenosis of 30%. 24 hours later, early follow-up angiography revealed persistent patency and unchanged lesion diameter of the target vessel. The patient was asymptomatic during the 2-month follow-up period, but 63 days after the procedure, he died suddenly while playing in a tennis tournament. Restenosis of 80% at the site of the lesion, without plaque rupture or thrombosis, was revealed by post-mortem histological examination. Significant proliferation of smooth muscle cells at the site of excimer laser coronary angioplasty was revealed by specific staining of the histological specimen for smooth muscle cells using alpha-actin. However, underlying fibrous plaque resulting from insufficient tissue ablation appeared to be the major cause of vessel narrowing. The size of currently available catheters, which are too small to create a large channel, was likely to blame for this.

Lingual exfoliative cytologic (scrapings) were obtained in 18 human immunodeficiency virus-positive patients with clinical oral hairy leukoplakia.  
In 12 of these patients, oral mucosal scrapings were obtained.  
For examination by transmission electron microscopy (TEM), the specimens were processed.  
Infection of keratinocytes with a herpes-like virus was revealed in sixteen (89%) of the lingual samples.  
In the 12 scrapings of the oral mucosa, there was no evidence of viral infection.  
By TEM, fungal hyphae were observed in 14 (78%) of the lingual scrapings and two (17%) of the oral scrapings.  
To detect Epstein-Barr virus DNA with a DNA probe, one exfoliative sample and two biopsy samples were stained.  
A direct and objective diagnosis allows the detection of herpes-type virions by TEM in the keratinocytes of a lesion clinically suspected of being hairy leukoplakia.  
The use of exfoliative cytological samples, moreover, constitutes a clinically simple and non-invasive technique.
